correctness.rationale: Three-move EF equivalence reduces to one-round ordered-pair extension profiles because every Cartesian clique product is vertex-transitive. Direct counting gives common-neighbor numbers \(q_i-2\) for an edge, 2 at Hamming distance two, and 0 at larger distance, with corresponding exclusive-neighbor and common-nonneighbor counts. Exact inequalities in \(N=\prod_iq_i\) and \(\Delta=\sum_i(q_i-1)\) split all products into nine mutually distinct signatures. The sharp minimal product sizes are 2,3,4,6,8,9,12,16,27. A standalone independent direct atomic-diagram enumeration matched the symbolic formula on 93 finite cases; the infinite claim depends on the proof, not the finite tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither assumption set includes the arbitrary unequal-factor products with \(d\ge3\). Their restriction to homogeneous alphabets or two factors cannot imply that every mixed high-dimensional product is rank-three equivalent to \(K_2\square K_2\square K_3\).

originality.rationale: Targeted research searches and source comparisons showed no stronger covering result. The accessible full text of Fisher and Isaak solves a two-factor automorphism/coloring problem, not rank-three logic; the visible older abstracts concern critical groups and Hamming subgraph characterizations. The closest identified homogeneous-product rank-four and two-factor all-rank logical results do not entail the mixed-factor, at-least-three-factor classification. Historical completeness is not claimed.

value.rationale: A natural unrestricted class—Cartesian products of complete graphs with arbitrary alphabet sizes—has its rank-three theories fully classified by nine structural parameter regimes and a sharp 27-vertex representative cutoff. In particular nonisomorphic mixed high-dimensional products collapse despite differing alphabet multisets, whereas the all-binary three-cube is separately visible because of one missing extension pattern. The exact boundary is motivated by bounded-depth expressive power, not an arbitrary finite parameter selection.
